questions.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the coordinates of the point ${A}^{′}$, the image of $A(-1,1)$ under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of $A$ under the action of $T$, we first create a column-vector $x$ containing the coordinates of $A:$

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $x$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $Tx:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Tx & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The result, $Tx,$ contains the coordinates of ${A}^{′}.$ Therefore, ${A}^{′}(2,1).$

questions.problem:
Consider the line $y=-\frac{2}{3}x-3$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

In **standard form**, the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T$ is

{{field-1}}$=-81.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=-\frac{2}{3}x-3$ passes through the points $A(0,-3)$ and $B(3,-5)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $A$ and $B$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ -3 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ -3 & -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 7 \\ -6 & -13\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${A}^{′}(-3,-6)$ and ${B}^{′}(7,-13).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${A}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y+6 & =\frac{-13+6}{7-(-3)}(x+3) \\ y+6 & =-\frac{7}{10}(x+3)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we transform the equation of the line to standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}10y+60 & =-7x-21 \\ 7x+10y & =-81\end{aligned}
$$

$$

{{field-1}}$=-5.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=2x+1$ passes through the points $A(0,1)$ and $B(1,3)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $A$ and $B$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${A}^{′}(-1,1)$ and ${B}^{′}(0,5).$

Now, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${A}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}$ in point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-1 & =\frac{5-1}{0+1}(x+1) \\ y-1 & =4(x+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we transform the equation of the line to standard form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-1 & =4x+4 \\ 4x-y & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

To find the image of $B$ under the action of $\mathbf T,$ we first create a column vector $\mathbf{x}$ containing the coordinates of $B{:}$

$$

$$

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $\mathbf T?$

First, let's find two points on the given line. Substituting $x=0$ and $x=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0\, & \to \,y=3(0)-2=-2, \\ x=1\, & \to \,y=3(1)-2=1.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have two points on the line, $P(0,-2)$ and $Q(1,1).$

To find the images of $P$ and $Q$ under the action of $\mathbf T,$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of $P$ and $Q$ in its columns:

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $\mathbf T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are $P'(0,-2)$ and $Q'(-1,4).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through $P'$ and $Q'\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-2) & =\frac{4-(-2)}{-1-0}(x-0) \\ y+2 & =-6x \\ 6x+y+2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Image of a Line Given by an Equation in Standard Form
canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the line $5x-y-3=0$ and linear transformation $\mathbf T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $\mathbf T?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, let's find two points on the given line. Solving for $y,$ we get $y=5x-3,$ and substituting $x=0$ and $x=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0\, & \to \,y=5(0)-3=-3, \\ x=1\, & \to \,y=5(1)-3=2.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have two points on the line, $P(0,-3)$ and $Q(1,2).$

To find the images of $P$ and $Q$ under the action of $\mathbf T,$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of $P$ and $Q$ in its columns:

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $\mathbf T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ -6 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are $P'(-3,-6)$ and $Q'(-1,3).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through $P'$ and $Q'\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-6) & =\frac{3-(-6)}{-1-(-3)}(x-(-3)) \\ y+6 & =\frac{9}{2}(x+3) \\ 2y+12 & =9x+27 \\ 9x-2y+15 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
